app.name: DD2 Save Manager
game.running: Game running · restore and apply locked
notice.gameRunning.title: The game is running.
notice.gameRunning.text: You can still make backups, but restoring and editing saves has to wait until the game is closed.
notice.readOnly.title: Read-only.
notice.readOnly.text: This save has parts the program does not fully understand, so to be safe it will not write changes to it.
notice.stale.title: The save has changed.
notice.stale.text: The game or a restore changed the file, so the values on screen are the old ones.
empty.noSaves: No Dragon's Dogma 2 saves were found in Steam on this PC. Start the game, save once, then check again.
backup.title: Backups
backup.lede: A backup is a copy of every file in the save folder, kept on this PC. Before a restore or an edit, the saves as they were are backed up once more automatically.
backup.unreadable: Unreadable file (another account's save, or damaged)
backup.done: The current saves have been backed up.
backup.empty: No backups yet. "Back up now" above keeps a copy of the saves exactly as they are.
backup.emptyHidden: Only hidden automatic backups are here.
backup.restoreText: The current saves are backed up automatically first, then the save folder is replaced with the {when} backup.
backup.trashText: The {when} backup moves to the _trash folder inside the backups folder. No file is deleted.
backup.restored: Restored the {when} backup. The saves from before are in the automatic backups.
backup.trashed: The backup was moved to the trash folder.
edit.title: Edit a save
edit.lede: Pick the save to change. Once you apply your changes, they take effect the next time the game loads that save.
edit.noSaves: There is no game save to edit.
edit.discard: There are changes you have not applied. Discard them and open the other save?
edit.discardOnClose: There are changes you have not applied. Discard them and close?
apply.hint: Applying backs up the current save automatically, then overwrites it.
apply.done: Applied to the save. The save as it was is in the backups, marked "Auto · before edit".
blocked.inexact: This save cannot be edited because the program does not fully understand its layout.
blocked.gameRunning: The game is running, so nothing can be applied. Close the game and you can apply right away.
blocked.stale: The save changed while it was open. Reload it first.
blocked.invalid: Fix the values in the fields marked red.
money.title: Currency
game.title: Game mode
game.note: The game mode is shown here, not edited. To change it, use Options on the game's title screen. The game records the mode in several places across the save and the system data, and which of them it follows has not been confirmed, so this tool leaves it alone.
travel.title: Fast travel
travel.lede: The permanent portcrystals that stand in towns and outposts. Marking one as found lets you travel to it with a Ferrystone.
travel.note: Once applied, a portcrystal cannot be unmarked here (restoring the automatic backup does undo it). Jumping to places you have never reached can tangle the story in between, so it is fine to pick only the ones you need. Whether they show on the map and can be travelled to still has to be checked in the game. The portcrystals of the Norgan region are not included.
character.name: Name
character.basicNote.player: Changing the current vocation changes the vocation only; equipment stays as it is, so equip that vocation's weapon yourself in the game. The name on the load screen changes the next time the game saves.
character.basicNote.pawn: The name is visible to other players. Changing the current vocation changes the vocation only; equipment stays as it is, so equip that vocation's weapon yourself in the game.
character.growthNote: These are the internal growth values built up by levelling, in different units from the numbers the game shows. Raising the level alone does not raise the stats, so change the growth values too if you need them.
job.note: The game works out the vocation rank again from the total experience. A vocation you tick as unlocked can be picked right away as the current vocation under "Basics".
skills.note: Skills can be unlocked but not locked again (restoring the automatic backup does undo it). A weapon skill that has an upgraded form can be taken to that form. Maister skills and the skills and augments of the expansion are in the lists too; the expansion's EX skills are not handled here. Equip skills in the game.
skills.noData: The lists of skills and augments are read from your installed game files. They have not been read yet.
pawn.note: Inclinations and specializations are named as the game names them. How high affinity can go is not known, so only 0 to 999 is accepted.
plague.title: Dragonsplague
plague.note: Dragonsplague spreads from support pawns, so the support pawns in the party are listed as well. All this does is set stage and progress back to 0. From which stage it becomes dangerous is not known.
items.title: Items
items.removeBlocked: Unequip the item in the game first
items.note: Put weapons and armor one per slot. Kinds are worked out from ID ranges.
items.enhanceNote: "Enhanced" is how many times a smith has enhanced the piece (0 to 3). Steps you add go in as Vermundian smithing; pieces that have had the Wyrmfire enhancement are left alone. What this value means was worked out from saves, so change one piece first and check it in the game.
category.head: Head armor
names.firstRun: Reading names and icons from your installed game files. This takes a moment.
names.built: Read {items} item names from the game files.
names.builtWithIcons: Read {items} item names and {icons} icons from the game files.
names.state.ok: Item names, icons and skill lists were read from your installed game files.
names.state.missing: There is no name dictionary yet, so items are shown by ID. The button on the right reads it from the game files.
names.state.outdated: The game files have not been read again since the game was updated. If new items show up as IDs, use the button on the right.
names.state.no-icons: There are no item icons yet. The button on the right builds them from the game files.
looks.title: Appearance
looks.lede: Save a face and body as a preset file, then put it on another character or into another save. Worn equipment and the voice do not change. "Show sheet" lists a look as numbers you can follow in the game's own character editor.
looks.guests.title: Taking the look of another player's pawn:
looks.guests.some: There are {n} support pawn(s) in the party right now. Pick one under "Character" below and save it as a preset to put it on your own characters.
looks.guests.none: Hire that pawn in the game, save with it in the party, then open that save here: it appears under "Character" below as a support pawn. This save has no support pawn in the party.
looks.name: Preset name
looks.saved: Saved the look in this save as a preset.
looks.empty: No saved presets. Save a character's look above to start.
sheet.title: Appearance sheet: {name}
sheet.copied: Copied the whole sheet. Paste it into a text editor.
sheet.copyFailed: Could not copy. Click this window once and try again.
sheet.note: In the order of the game's character editor. Sliders are the numbers shown on screen; shapes and colours are given by their place in the list. Places follow the order in the game data and can be a step or two off on screen, so pick colours by comparing with the swatch.
sheet.unknown: Left out because they could not be read: {list}
sheet.outOfRangeHint: The game's slider cannot reach this value. Use the nearest end.
error.generic: The request could not be completed.
error.game-running: The game is running. Close it and try again.
error.stale: The save changed while it was open. Reload it, then edit.
error.wrong-account: This save was made by another Steam account and cannot be opened.
error.checksum: The save file is damaged and cannot be read.
error.signature: The save file is damaged and cannot be read.
error.truncated: The save file is damaged and cannot be read.
error.inexact: This save cannot be edited because the program does not fully understand its layout.
error.layout: This save is not laid out as expected. The game version may have changed.
error.range: A value is outside the allowed range.
error.full: The item storage is full; nothing more can be added.
error.equipped: Unequip the item in the game first.
error.look: This appearance preset does not fit this save.
error.token: This window is out of date. Start the program again.
error.not-found: It could not be found. It may already have been moved or removed.
error.empty: There are no save files to back up.
error.verify: The rebuilt save did not pass verification, so nothing was written.
error.no-saves: No Dragon's Dogma 2 saves were found on this PC.
error.no-game: The installed game was not found on this PC, so its files cannot be read.
error.no-names: No item names were found in the game files. A game update may have changed the files.
error.no-icons: No item icons were found in the game files.
error.no-editor: The character editor data was not found in the game files. A game update may have changed the files.
error.editor-layout: The game's character editor data is not as expected, so the sheet cannot be made. The game may have been updated.
error.no-skill-data: The skill lists have not been read from the game files yet. Use "Read game files again" first.
error.name: A name is 1 to 12 characters, without < or >.
error.job-locked: A vocation that is not unlocked cannot be taken. Unlock it under "Vocations" first.
error.no-character: That character was not found in this save. Reload the save.
error.unsupported: This edition does not have that feature.
